title: GCP Marketplace Listing Copy Draft (v2) — Redwood Inference
content:
Doc goal
- Produce a GCP Marketplace-ready copy set for Redwood Inference (v2). This doc includes: customer-facing copy blocks + internal differentiation notes + placeholders for required visuals.
- Audience: procurement-led enterprise buyers + engineers evaluating inference runtime economics (latency/cost/reliability).

Status / what changed in v2
- Reframed top section around “production-grade inference economics” (latency, cost, reliability) vs generic “model access.”
- Clarified deployment modes: Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private (VPC/on‑prem) — without overspecifying terms that require legal review.
- Added a cleaner “How it works on Marketplace” flow (subscribe → entitlement → Redwood org provisioning → API key → meter/invoice).
- Added security section written to pass marketplace review; avoids absolute claims (e.g., “ISO certified”) unless confirmed.

------------------------------------------------------------
LISTING COPY (CUSTOMER-FACING)

Proposed Listing Name (GCP Marketplace)
- Redwood Inference — Production LLM Inference (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)

Tagline (1 line)
- Run and optimize LLM inference with predictable latency, cost controls, and flexible deployment options.

Short description (marketplace card)
- Developer-first LLM inference platform delivering high-throughput serving, observability, and cost optimization across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Long description (overview)
Redwood Inference helps engineering teams ship LLM-powered applications with predictable performance in production. Redwood provides a unified inference runtime and operational tooling to control latency and unit economics while maintaining reliability and deployment flexibility.

Choose the deployment model that matches your requirements:
- Hosted API: fastest time-to-value, usage-based billing
- Dedicated capacity: reserved throughput and data isolation for steady production workloads
- Private deployment: VPC and on-prem options for regulated or network-restricted environments

Redwood includes production-grade capabilities like smart routing, continuous batching, caching, model lifecycle controls (version pinning and rollouts), and token-level observability to help you find and fix performance regressions.

Key benefits
- Lower latency and higher throughput: GPU-optimized serving runtime with workload-aware batching and KV/prefix caching
- Cost controls with visibility: token-level cost and latency breakdowns, plus recommendations to reduce spend
- Reliability and graceful degradation: routing policies and fallback options to keep apps online
- Deployment flexibility: consistent API and tooling across hosted, dedicated, and private environments

Key features
1) Inference API surface
- Text generation and chat
- Embeddings and reranking
- Streaming responses
- Structured output and tool/function calling support (where model-compatible)

2) Operations and observability (Console)
- Per-model and per-route latency + error dashboards
- Token-level usage analytics
- Tracing hooks (integration-dependent)
- Rollouts: canary, A/B tests, and fallback policies

3) Performance and cost optimization (Optimize)
- Workload-aware batching and caching configuration suggestions
- Model and quantization profile recommendations by workload
- Quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to evaluation prompt sets

How it works (Marketplace onboarding)
1) Subscribe in Google Cloud Marketplace
2) Redwood validates your subscription entitlement
3) Provision or link your Redwood organization
4) Create your first API key in the Redwood Console
5) Send your first request using Redwood SDKs or REST
6) Usage is metered to your marketplace billing account per your selected SKU/dimensions

Supported deployment options (what you’re buying)
- Hosted API via Marketplace: usage-based metering aligned to your selected dimension(s)
- Dedicated capacity via Marketplace (where applicable): committed spend / reserved capacity offer structure (typically sales-assisted)
- Private deployments: available via private offer / enterprise engagement (details vary by environment and requirements)

Recommended use cases
- SaaS product teams adding chat, summarization, extraction, and agentic workflows to existing applications
- AI-native startups that need low-latency inference and cost control with a simple API
- Enterprises with procurement requirements for Marketplace purchasing and consolidated billing
- Regulated workloads that need private networking and enhanced audit logging

Security and compliance (high-level)
- Encryption in transit (TLS) and encryption at rest for platform-managed storage (service-dependent)
- Customer data isolation options via Dedicated capacity and Private deployments
- Audit logging available for key administrative and access events (export options available depending on plan)
- SOC 2 Type II report available upon request (under NDA) and controls aligned to common ISO 27001 expectations
- Shared responsibility model: Redwood secures the platform; customers secure their applications, prompts, and access policies

Support
- Standard support included; enterprise support and SLA options available for Dedicated and Private
- Support channels: ticketing + email; escalation path for entitlement/provisioning issues

Call to action
- Subscribe to get started, then follow the onboarding steps to provision your Redwood org and create an API key.
- For Dedicated capacity or Private deployments, contact Sales from the listing to discuss requirements and offer structure.

------------------------------------------------------------
FAQ (DRAFT)

Q: What do I get immediately after subscribing?
A: You can link or provision a Redwood organization, create an API key, and start making Hosted API requests. Some Dedicated/Private options require a sales-assisted flow.

Q: How does billing work through GCP Marketplace?
A: Usage is metered and billed through your Google Cloud billing account based on the SKU and billing dimensions you select. Redwood’s console provides usage analytics for transparency.

Q: Can I use my existing Redwood account?
A: Yes. During onboarding you can link an existing Redwood org (if you have the right permissions) or create a new org.

Q: What if entitlement provisioning is delayed?
A: Entitlement propagation may take time. The console provides retry guidance and support contact steps if verification doesn’t complete within the expected window.

Q: Do you store prompts or model outputs?
A: Redwood’s data handling depends on configuration and deployment mode. Refer to the Redwood security documentation for retention defaults and configurable controls.

Q: Is customer-managed encryption key (CMEK) supported?
A: Available for certain Dedicated/Private configurations. Confirm requirements during sales-assisted scoping.

Q: What regions are supported?
A: Region availability depends on deployment mode and selected offer. Use the onboarding flow to select from supported regions.

------------------------------------------------------------
DIFFERENTIATION NOTES (INTERNAL — NOT FOR LISTING)

Primary positioning pillars (approved)
- Production economics: predictable latency, throughput, and unit cost controls
- Reliability + graceful degradation: routing/fallback when capacity is constrained
- Unified runtime + tooling across Hosted/Dedicated/Private

Avoid / do not say (unless cleared)
- Avoid “cheapest” / “best” / “guaranteed” performance claims.
- Avoid claiming ISO 27001 certification unless verified.
- Avoid naming competitors directly in listing copy.
- Avoid promising 0 data retention; talk about configurable retention and the shared responsibility model.

Differentiation vs typical GCP alternatives (talking points for Sales/SE, not listing)
- Compared to generic managed endpoints: Redwood focuses on inference optimization + per-token observability + routing/fallback policies.
- Compared to “simple LLM APIs”: Redwood supports enterprise deployment modes (Dedicated/Private) and operational controls (rollouts, eval regression monitoring).

Open questions / items to confirm (blocking before final)
- Exact GCP Marketplace dimensions and naming (needs final from SKU catalog + billing mapping).
- Support language: what is “standard” vs “enterprise” support by SKU.
- Security text: confirm what is public vs gated (SOC 2 availability language, audit log details, retention defaults).
- Region list: decide whether we list a subset publicly or reference “see docs/console.”
